title: SLO-aware elastic shear throttle for continuous batching
creator: Priya Khanna
description:
Summary: Implement an "elastic shear throttle" — a soft, SLO-aware preemption policy for continuous batching that reduces eviction thrash, smooths tenant throughput during KV pressure, and enforces latency SLOs with minimal tail-regression.

Goal: Provide a heuristic-driven throttle that: 1) detects incoming KV-memory pressure and growing tail latency; 2) applies graded, tenant-scoped "shear" (gradual reduction) of batch admission and slot allocation; 3) preferentially preserves active KV working sets for units approaching completion; and 4) integrates with routing fallbacks to keep high-priority tenants within SLOs.

Why this is different: Existing preemption strategies are often binary (interrupt / don't interrupt) or rely on hard quotas that cause abrupt evictions and cold-starts in the KV cache. Elastic shear throttle aims to produce smoother degradation (less oscillation), reduce repeated KV evictions, and maintain better overall GPU memory utilization under mixed workloads.

Acceptance criteria: 
- End-to-end tests show <=5% increase in P95 latency for tier-1 (SLO-bound) tenants under 95th percentile KV pressure compared to baseline, while decreasing KV eviction churn by >=20%.
- No regression in throughput for non-SLO tenants > 10% for sustained 5-minute pressure windows.
- New metric set exposed in Console: "shear_applied_pct", "shear_window_seconds", "kv_eviction_churn_rate".
- Feature flag gated and rolloutable by tenant and region.

Design notes / algorithm sketch: 
- Inputs: per-tenant latency SLOs, current batch queue lengths, per-batch KV-residency footprint estimate, GPU free memory, recent KV eviction rate, and time-since-last-eviction-per-tenant.
- Output: per-tenant admission multiplier in [0.0, 1.0] applied to continuous batch admission and slot sizing.
- Core heuristic: compute a transient "stress_score" = weighted(sum of normalized eviction_rate, normalized tail_latency_delta, normalized free_memory_delta). Map stress_score via a sigmoid-shaped curve to an admission multiplier to avoid step changes.
- Soft guarantees: priority & SLO tiers get bounded minimum multiplier (e.g., 0.3) while best-effort tenants can be reduced to 0.0.
- KV-aware preservation: if a tenant's active requests are near completion (kv_cache_hit_ratio rising and remaining_token_estimate small), temporarily prioritize their admission to avoid cache thrash.
- Backoff: multipliers decay back to 1.0 with hysteresis windows and a small randomized jitter to prevent synchronized oscillation across GPUs.

Trade-offs considered: 
- Complexity vs observability: more signals improve behavior but increase surface area for bugs. We cap inputs to 6 signals and expose feature toggles.
- Strict fairness vs SLO preservation: chosen to bias slightly toward preserving latency SLOs for configured tiers.
- Heuristic vs learned policy: we prefer deterministic heuristics for predictability in the first rollout. Future follow-up could explore RL/OPA-based controllers.

Rollout plan: 
1) Implement algorithm behind feature flag and unit tests (dev).
2) Canary on dedicated pool in us-west-2 with synthetic KV pressure jobs (internal perf job).
3) Monitor metrics for 48 hours; if KV eviction churn decreases and P95 stays within threshold, enable for 10 production tenants.
4) Gradual ramp to all non-government tiers over 2 weeks with automated rollback.

Observability / Metrics required: 
- shear_applied_pct per-tenant (histogram)
- kv_eviction_churn_rate per-GPU
- tenant_tail_latency_delta (P95 delta relative to baseline)
- gpu_free_memory_seconds (time spent under warning threshold)
- preemption_count_by_tenant and preemption_duration

Testing: 
- Unit tests for mapping curve edge cases and hysteresis behavior.
- Integration tests using the perf harness to simulate mixed workloads with different SLO mixes and KV footprints.
- Chaos test: inject KV eviction spikes and measure hysteresis/jitter stability.

Implementation tasks (checklist): 
- [x] proto: local simulation harness and synthetic KV-pressure generator (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2483)
- [ ] core: implement admission multiplier pipeline in continuous-batcher module and expose feature flag (target: runtime-1.19 branch)
- [ ] tests: unit and integration test coverage for boundary conditions
- [ ] metrics: add telemetry exports and Console dashboard stub (telemetry PR: github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/1012)
- [ ] rollout: canary config and automation script for rollback

Risks & mitigations: 
- Risk: misconfiguration leads to over-throttling causing customer-visible errors. Mitigation: feature flag default off, conservative minimum multipliers for SLO tiers, and automatic rollback if P99 increases by >20%.
- Risk: coordination across GPUs (synchronized jitter) causes oscillation. Mitigation: per-GPU seed + small randomized jitter; increase hysteresis if needed.
- Risk: hidden interaction with existing quota system. Mitigation: integration tests and a short-lived compatibility shim that translates multiplier into existing quota units.

Related artifacts: 
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Elastic+Shear+Throttle+Design 
- Perf harness PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2483 
- Telemetry dashboard stub: github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/734 

Notes / decisions so far: 
- Decided to use sigmoid mapping instead of linear clamp to avoid abrupt cutovers (2025-02-24, decision by Priya + Mateo + Lina).
- Opted for deterministic heuristic for initial rollout; follow-up ticket will evaluate learned policy based on canary telemetry (see sub_issues).

Subsequent work / follow-ups (sub_issues): 
- ENG-88201: Evaluate ML-based admission controller (post-canary)
- ENG-88311: Tunable KV-preservation heuristics and tenant-level config UI
